_PROJECT_HOOK: ===== PROJECT HOOK: map these preset knobs to YOUR device build flags/macros =====
_how_to_fill: The three presets (off / entry_only / full) are the canonical profiler build modes. Fill compile_defines/compile_flags with the actual preprocessor macros or build args your kernel uses to gate profiling. run_profile.py passes the selected preset name; validate_overhead.py times off vs entry_only vs full using these. Keep the names and semantics; only the flag values are project-specific.
name: off
description: Profiler fully compiled out. Zero device-side recording, zero buffer traffic. This is the timing baseline for overhead measurement and the correctness reference build.
_compile_defines_note: The KEY is a project hook, not just the value. A macro name that does not exist in your device source still compiles cleanly — it simply gates nothing — so a copied-verbatim name produces a build that looks fine and records nothing (or records everything in the 'off' baseline, which silently deflates the measured overhead). Grep your device source for the real `#ifdef` / `if constexpr` guard names and use those exact spellings.
_compile_flags_note: Empty is only correct if your 'off' build needs no extra compiler/build args beyond the defines above. Verify by building with this preset and confirming the profiler symbols are absent; do not assume.
_expected_overhead_note: 0.0 here is definitional, not measured: 'off' IS the baseline this ratio is measured against. The other two presets must carry a real measured number from validate_overhead.py, never a guess.
